cosy-lesson.title: Oh My God I Think I Like You

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Panic – Sudden uncontrollable fear or anxiety, often causing wildly unthinking behavior.

p.em: Example: Realizing you have genuine feelings for a casual hookup induces pure panic.

cosy-blockquote.p: Vulnerable – Exposed to the possibility of being attacked or harmed, either physically or emotionally.

p.em: Example: Admitting you care about someone makes you feel terrified and vulnerable.

cosy-blockquote.p: Casual – Relaxed and unconcerned; not formal or serious.

p.em: Example: They agreed to keep their relationship strictly casual, but emotions intervened.

cosy-blockquote.p: Horrified – Filled with horror; extremely shocked or dismayed.

p.em: Example: She was horrified to discover that sweet romantic thoughts had entered her head.

cosy-blockquote.p: Affection – A gentle feeling of liking or fondness.

p.em: Example: Unwanted affection can catch you completely off guard during a simple conversation.

cosy-blockquote.p: Denial – The action of declaring something to be untrue; refusal to accept reality.

p.em: Example: She stayed in complete denial until her heart started racing around him.

cosy-blockquote.p: Accidental – Happening by chance, unintentionally, or unexpectedly.

p.em: Example: An accidental moment of genuine warmth shattered her cynical rules.

cosy-blockquote.p: Overwhelmed – Completely overcome in mind or feeling by a superior force.

p.em: Example: Feeling overwhelmed by unexpected intimacy is a common dater experience.

cosy-blockquote.p: Complicated – Consisting of many interconnecting parts or elements; intricate.

p.em: Example: What started as a simple physical arrangement quickly became deeply complicated.

cosy-blockquote.p: Terrified – Cause to feel extreme fear.

p.em: Example: She was terrified of ruining her independent lifestyle for love.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Share whether you agree or disagree with these statements and discuss them with your teacher:

ul.li: Incorrect: She is terrified about falling in love → Correct: She is terrified of falling in love ((Use 'terrified of + -ing'.))
Incorrect: He is vulnerable for emotional pain → Correct: He is vulnerable to emotional pain ((Use 'vulnerable to'.))
Incorrect: They are in denial for their feelings → Correct: They are in denial about their feelings ((Use 'in denial about'.))
